problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=9xy$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=16,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $4$ and $\frac{4}{3},$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+\frac{16}{9}{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=9xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =9\cdot 4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t=48\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}9xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }48\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =64{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=8{sin}^{2}⁡t+1,$ $\text{d}u=16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}64{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t & =4{\int }_{1}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{1} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
